acceptance_criteria.reference: NSC-025 AC-001; GDD - 2.5D Isometric Visual and World Representation
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Update Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Editor/DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs so, after DoorSequenceBuilder.BuildCanonical has composed the room scenes, it creates a persistent builder-owned GameplayNavigation GameObject. The navigation component on that GameObject must bake one walkable NavMesh from the composed gameplay collision geometry, including the room FloorCollision and obstacle colliders, while excluding the visual Tilemaps as gameplay truth. Rebuilding the scene must remove and recreate this owned GameObject deterministically.

Create Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/World/GameplayNavigationSurface.cs as the runtime component that owns and configures Unity AI Navigation's NavMeshSurface, and add the Unity.AI.Navigation reference to Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.asmdef. The component and test-owned NavMeshAgent must use the same project-configured agent type and its radius, height, and slope settings. Do not edit ProjectSettings or the Editor asmdef. Create Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Tests/Editor/NavMeshAgentConfigurationTests.cs for the configuration and navigation validation in VAL-001.

completion_gates.reference: NSC-025 VAL-002 (walkable NavMesh prerequisite); GDD - Runtime Implementation
completion_gates.requirement: The Edit Mode test Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Tests/Editor/NavMeshAgentConfigurationTests.cs uses a fresh in-memory scene to verify GameplayNavigationSurface configuration and that a test-owned NavMeshAgent using the selected agent type finds a complete path across a test-owned open gameplay floor. That check does not prove canonical room composition. After the authorized No Safe Circle/Build Door Prototype Scene command materializes Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity in the isolated task checkout, validate the built canonical scene without saving or changing it: the five-room composition has removed the legacy Floor, exactly one builder-owned GameplayNavigation and GameplayNavigationSurface survive, navigation uses the composed FloorCollision and obstacle colliders rather than visual Tilemaps, and a configured test-owned NavMeshAgent finds a complete path across open composed gameplay floor after scene load or the specified runtime rebuild. Repeat the authorized builder materialization and recheck that exactly one navigation owner remains and the composed-floor path still works. Validation-only tests must not save or modify the committed canonical scene.

children.decomposition_reason: This child owns the approved Unity AI Navigation package connection, the persistent scene-level NavMeshSurface, deterministic baking from gameplay collision, and the agent configuration used by enemy movement. A runtime wrapper keeps package-dependent code inside the authorized runtime assembly while the existing Editor builder creates and invokes that component.

downstream_integration_obligations.reference: NSC-025 INT-001; NSC-071 Bone Archive Navigation Lane Validation
downstream_integration_obligations.requirement: After this task's NavMesh agent configuration and NSC-045's authored Bone Archive geometry are available, NSC-071 validates that an enemy using the configured agent can traverse the committed BA-1 2.5-unit pinch and every intended Bone Archive lane. A synthetic corridor does not satisfy that room-specific proof.

children.execution_reason: One agent can add the named runtime NavMeshSurface component, connect it to the existing scene builder after room composition, configure one agent type, and add the focused non-saving Edit Mode test. The controller can then run No Safe Circle/Build Door Prototype Scene to materialize the authorized canonical scene output.

gdd_evidence.requirement: A shared gameplay navigation/locomotion layer owns the walkable movement representation and navigation-facing configuration used by runtime movers, and owns the navigation-side implementation of the shared door-passability interface.
The approved implementation uses Unity AI Navigation (com.unity.ai.navigation) and NavMesh-based runtime movement, while gameplay collision and walkability remain separate from the visual layer.

gdd_evidence.reference: GDD - 2.5D Isometric Visual and World Representation
gdd_evidence.requirement: A minimal working navigation/locomotion layer and the approved package configuration must exist before locomotion-dependent enemy implementation is dispatched.

DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder remains the source of truth for the generated GameplayNavigation GameObject and Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity; the implementation worker must not hand-edit the serialized scene as a substitute for running the Unity builder.

acceptance_criteria.reference: NSC-025 AC-003; GDD - Door and Pursuit Rules (door passability contract)
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Create Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/World/DoorEnemyPassability.cs with a public method that accepts the sealed, open, locked, or broken semantic state supplied by Door and Interaction. The component must make its doorway block enemy NavMesh traversal while sealed or locked and allow enemy traversal through the opening while open or broken. It does not own or change DoorInteractable's current door state.

DoorEnemyPassability.cs must implement one Unity navigation mechanism behind its public method, such as NavMesh obstacle carving, a navigation link, or a runtime NavMesh-data update. DoorInteractable, enemy pursuit code, and other callers must not manipulate that NavMesh mechanism directly. Create Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Tests/DoorEnemyPassabilityPlayModeTests.cs for the required runtime path checks.

completion_gates.reference: NSC-025 VAL-002; GDD - Door and Pursuit Rules (door passability contract)
completion_gates.requirement: In Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Tests/DoorEnemyPassabilityPlayModeTests.cs, build a test-owned NavMesh floor and doorway with GameplayNavigationSurface, place a test-owned NavMeshAgent on the approach side, and request a path to the forward side after publishing each semantic door state. Verify that sealed and locked prevent a complete path through the opening, while open and broken allow a complete path. The test must use temporary scene objects and must not save Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity.

children.decomposition_reason: The GDD fixes the four door-state results while leaving the Unity NavMesh mechanism to the implementation agent. This child can implement and test that navigation-owned component after the sibling NavMeshSurface component exists; connecting real DoorInteractable state changes remains assigned to NSC-051.
children.execution_reason: One agent can implement the named navigation-owned door-passability component and prove the four pathing results with a temporary Play Mode fixture. It does not edit DoorInteractable, the canonical scene, or the scene builder.

inbound_dependency_rewrites.reason: NSC-013 applies Frost movement slowdown and forced displacement while preserving valid enemy navigation state. It uses the shared NavMesh representation and agent configuration but does not use door semantic-state publication.

NSC-014 uses the shared NavMesh representation for enemy pursuit and search movement, and it uses the door-passability result when an enemy crosses an open or broken doorway. Its contract therefore uses both children.

NSC-021 is a non-executable Door aggregate. Its NSC-025 dependency supports the navigation-owned interface used by child NSC-051, so the aggregate dependency is replaced by the door-passability component; that child already depends locally on the NavMeshSurface child.

NSC-051 connects real DoorInteractable sealed, open, locked, broken, initialization, and reset state changes to the navigation-owned component. It uses the door-passability child and does not own NavMeshSurface or agent configuration.

NSC-071 validates the configured enemy agent on committed Bone Archive geometry, including the BA-1 pinch and intended lanes. It uses the NavMeshSurface and agent configuration, not door-state switching.

NSC-088 requires a travelling phantom to move along an available corridor, so its existing NSC-025 dependency is replaced by the NavMesh representation child. Its door traversal remains an unresolved human design decision, and the current contract does not authorize use of the enemy-only door-passability component.

reason: NSC-025 contains two separately testable Unity responsibilities: building the shared NavMeshSurface and agent configuration used by enemy movement, and implementing the navigation-owned component that turns Door and Interaction's four semantic states into blocked or passable enemy paths. The first child creates a persistent navigation GameObject after the canonical five-room composition and uses a named runtime wrapper so no unlisted Editor asmdef edit is needed. The second child depends on that NavMesh component and owns only door-state-to-pathing behavior. Existing NSC-051 remains the explicit task that connects real DoorInteractable state changes to the navigation component.
